banner.title: Built for players, shaped by play
banner.text: Every project starts with a playable prototype. We test early with real players, keep what is fun and cut what is not, so the final game feels right from the very first minute.
banner.alt: Close-up of an anime character with snow in the hair

services.title: Everything a game needs, under one roof
services.text: Art, code, sound and live operations are handled by one team, so nothing gets lost between hand-offs. Pick a single service or let us take the project from concept to release.

about.title: A studio built by players, for players
about.lead: Logo started in 2012 as five friends making mobile games after work. Today we are a global studio shipping 3D games on every major platform.
about.slide1Alt: Character standing in a neon-lit city street
about.slide2Alt: Warrior with a glowing sword in a teal-lit hall

craft.title: Quality you can feel
craft.text: Every build goes through art, gameplay and performance reviews, so polish is part of the process and never a last-minute rush.

people.title: Teams that stay together
people.text: Most of our developers have been with us for years. Stable teams know the codebase, the pipeline and each other, and it shows in the result.

reach.title: Global, yet close
reach.text: With 18 offices we work in your time zone and speak your language, while sharing tools and standards across every studio.

story.label: Our story
story.title: From a shared apartment to a global studio
story.text: Logo began in 2012 with five friends and one very loud shared apartment. Our first mobile game found a loyal audience, and the studio grew one project at a time: PC, consoles, then AR and VR. Today we still start every project the same way, with a playable idea and honest feedback from players.

n1.title: Meet the neon dragon: how our newest art style came together
n1.author: Anna Petrova
n1.p0: Our new art direction began as a single paint-over on a Friday afternoon. Within a week the whole team was sketching glowing dragons, and the look quickly became the backbone of the next game's world. We kept the shapes bold, the colours saturated and the lighting dramatic, so that every frame works as a poster.
n1.p1: Next up: turning the concept into real-time characters without losing the painted feel.

n2.title: Night streets, real rain: building a city players want to get lost in
n2.alt: Character standing in a neon-lit city street
n2.author: Daniel Moreno
n2.p0: We built the street from reference photos of night markets, then spent weeks on wet surfaces, neon reflections and small details such as the cat by the shop window. The goal was a place that feels lived in, where players slow down just to look around.
